one_liner: Zig WebAssembly interpreter with a C API; roughly level with WAMR fast-interp and ahead of Wasmtime Pulley, behind wasm3.
what_it_does: An embeddable WebAssembly runtime (interpreter only, no JIT or AOT tier) written in Zig, with a CLI, a Zig API (Engine, Module, Store, Instance), a C API (libwasmz plus wasmz.h, shared or static) and Rust bindings added in August 2026. It targets Wasm 3.0 features (GC, SIMD, legacy and exnref exception handling, memory64, threads/atomics, tail calls) plus WASI Preview 1 in the CLI and Zig API. The C API is its own small wasmz_* interface (engine/store/module/instance/linker), not the standard wasm-c-api, so it is not a drop-in for WAMR or wasm3 embeddings.
how_it_is_fast: Each function's stack bytecode is lowered to a register IR with 16-bit slot operands, then executed with direct threaded code: every encoded op carries an 8-byte handler pointer and each handler tail-calls the next, spreading branch prediction across dispatch sites. A wasm3-style accumulator pair (r0 for integers, fp0 for floats) keeps the last result in a hardware register, and a peephole pass fuses common patterns into superinstructions (const+binop, compare+branch, binop+local.set, local in-place update, call_leaf). Functions compile lazily on first call, the .wasm file is mmapped, and linear memory is a PROT_NONE reservation committed on memory.grow.
when_to_use: You need a pure interpreter (no executable memory, e.g. iOS/App Store or watchOS) that runs Wasm 3.0 modules using GC, memory64 or exception handling; in the independent harness it was the fastest runtime on the memory64, EH-parser and GC rows.
Large modules where only part of the code runs: lazy per-function compilation makes start-up of a 19 MB module (esbuild) cheap compared with eager translators.
Scalar MVP code where WAMR fast-interp is the alternative: the two are within a few percent on M4 E-cores (geomean 1.59 vs 1.63).
Zig projects, or C/C++/Rust hosts that are fine with a small custom C API and are willing to supply their own host imports.
when_not_to_use: Peak interpreter speed on MVP code: wasm3 v0.9.0 was about 1.6x faster in the independent harness (geomean 1.01 vs 1.59 on M4 E-cores), and WAMR was faster on the A12 (1.38 vs 1.63).

Untrusted modules: issue #8 (open) reports that spec-invalid modules (bad subtype hierarchies, wrong operand-stack types, wrong result arity) are accepted and run, and the August 2026 history includes silent miscompiles and out-of-bounds address bugs (#1, #2, #10, #12).

Auto-vectorized (v128) code: v0.1.4 segfaulted on the SIMD builds of sieve and crc32, and extended-const initializers, catch_ref/throw_ref and expression-form elem segments gave wrong results or traps.
Long-lived instances that allocate GC objects: GC structs are never collected while the instance lives (316 MB peak on gc_trees), despite the README's 'automatic memory management'.
Multi-memory modules (rejected at compile) or C API callers that need multi-value results (the C API returns at most one value).

integration.form: static lib or shared lib (C API via zig build clib / static-lib), Zig module, Rust crate bindings
integration.dependencies: none beyond the Zig standard library (a small refcount library, zigrc, is vendored under src/libs)
integration.platforms: Linux, macOS, Windows release builds; x86-64 and aarch64 (full LTO on Linux for both), 32-bit targets fixed in June 2026; iOS and arm64_32 watchOS built by the independent harness (watchOS with a carried patch); can also compile itself to wasm32-wasi
integration.thread_safety: Engine and Module refcounts are thread-safe and a compiled Module can be shared; Store and Instance are not thread-safe, so use one Store/Instance per thread (docs/src/c-api.md).
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — the CLI runs WASI command modules like wasmtime/iwasm, but the C API is a custom wasmz_* API (not wasm-c-api) and does not expose WASI, so embedders of WAMR or Pulley must rewrite their host glue.

gotchas: First-party harness flaw: bench/bench.sh times whole processes with hyperfine and never checks program output; the QuickJS and esbuild RSS rows measure the 'sh -c' wrapper's PID (1.8 MB for every runtime), so those memory numbers are invalid; wasmz is built by Zig for the native CPU with full LTO while wasm3 (an old v0.5.1) and WAMR use generic cmake builds.

The numbers in docs/src/bench.md (2026-04-16) predate the August 2026 miscompilation fixes ('keep operand-stack reads of a local independent of later writes', 'only rename a label slot onto the temporary that a branch consumes'), so they were measured on code later fixed for correctness bugs.

WASI Preview 1 lives in the CLI and Zig API; the C API (wasmz.h) has no WASI entry points, so C/C++ hosts must register wasi_snapshot_preview1 imports themselves through wasmz_linker_define_func (host functions only landed in the C API on 2026-08-13).

'make build' (labelled recommended) is ReleaseSafe with -Dprofiling=true; the benchmarked configuration is 'make release' (ReleaseFast), which also drops Zig's runtime safety checks (a ReleaseFast-only fd_write bug was fixed in July 2026).
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick wasm3 for the fastest MVP interpretation (about 1.6x faster here) and WAMR fast-interp for maturity and the A12-class cores; pick wasmz over them when you need GC, memory64 or both exception-handling flavours in an interpreter, where wasm3 has none and the WAMR build in that harness had no GC or memory64. Against Wasmi and Pulley it trades a smaller, simpler C-callable runtime for less validation and a younger codebase.
verified_claims_summary: The independent rebeckerspecialties/wasm-benchmark run (2026-09-22; wasmz v0.1.4 static lib, Zig 0.16.0 ReleaseFast; C runtimes with Apple clang 21 -O3 -mcpu=apple-a12; N=10) gives CPU time per call relative to the per-case fastest runtime, geomean over 17 shared cases: M4 Max E-cores wasmz 1.59 vs WAMR fast-interp 1.63, Wasmtime Pulley 2.09, wasm3 1.01; iPhone XS (A12) E-cores 1.63 vs WAMR 1.38, Pulley 1.68, wasm3 1.04. The repo's own report (2026-04-16, Linux 6.17 Azure x86_64, CPU model not stated, hyperfine whole-process medians) shows fib(30) 37.0 ms vs wasmi 38.4, wasm3 v0.5.1 39.7, WAMR 49.6 and QuickJS fib(25) 174.9 ms vs 184.4/217.4/242.9.
status_note: Active single-author project (272 commits, last push 2026-08-17, Rust bindings just added), MIT and small enough to vendor, but at 0.1.x with an open spec-validation gap and six failing rows in the independent harness it is best treated as experimental for untrusted or SIMD-heavy modules.
